# Game Over Online — contemporary review

- Original source: [Game Over Online — contemporary review](https://www.game-over.com/reviews/pc/Robin_Hood%3A_The_Legend_of_Sherwood.html)
- Author / publication: Westlake / Game Over Online
- Language / date: English; 2003-02-24
- Access: Full review page retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: [Wayback Machine, 2025-10-31](http://web.archive.org/web/20251031204011/https://www.game-over.com/reviews/pc/Robin_Hood:_The_Legend_of_Sherwood.html)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial review, not transcribed)

**Score: 79%.**

This review is more reserved than GameSpot and WorthPlaying. It views Robin Hood as competent but less imaginative than Desperados and Commandos, particularly compared with Desperados' more flamboyant presentation.

Its opening outlines the ransom premise: Robin accumulates money to free Richard rather than simply distributing everything to the poor. The score breakdown awards 34/40 for gameplay, 13/15 for graphics, 12/15 for sound, 7/10 for interface, 7/10 for story, 2/5 for technical quality, and 4/5 for documentation.

**Research use:** a counterpoint to strongly favorable launch reviews and a pointer to contemporary technical concerns. The low technical subscore alone does not identify a specific bug.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: review of the Strategy First release; listed requirements Windows, Pentium II 233, 64 MB RAM, 900 MB HDD, 4× CD-ROM; rating 79%; posted Monday 24 February 2003 11:18 AM; author Westlake; ten screenshots. Sub-scores: gameplay 34/40, graphics 13/15, sound 12/15, interface 7/10, storyline 7/10, technical 2/5, documentation 4/5. Commercial review text, so paraphrased.

- Frames the game as Spellbound's follow-up to Desperados (summer 2001), itself indebted to Pyro's Commandos (1998); the reviewer finds Robin Hood competent but "curiously flat and unimaginative" next to Desperados.
- Premise: Richard has been kidnapped, so Robin keeps the money for the ransom instead of giving it to the poor.
- Character abilities noted: Robin expert bowman who distracts by throwing gold; Little John's staff and body carrying; Marian heals; Friar Tuck ties people up; Will Scarlet knocks out with a slingshot.
- Nonlethal play: the game penalises killing slightly; Robin and Little John punch to knock out, and the staff always knocks out; because Robin's own weapons (sword, bow) kill, the reviewer used him little after the first missions.
- New systems: Sherwood as base where those left behind train, heal, fletch arrows or pick herbs; characters gain experience, but only through training in Sherwood, never from fighting, which the reviewer calls flaky.
- Campaign criticism: about 30 missions on only eight maps (five castles, three forests); every forest mission is an ambush of a gold shipment or tax collector; every main character gets captured, yielding over half a dozen rescue missions; no multiplayer and no scenario editor, so the campaign is everything.
- Technical: saves and loads are nearly instant; but an apparent memory leak caused freezes, crashes and reboots; zooming froze the machine so often he stopped; forest maps flickered; three months after release no substantial patch.
- Verdict: enjoyed about 40 hours, recommends it, notes a street price of about $20.
